verse.reading: The one that was first became forms upon forms, rose as the differences of caste and became every living being; after staying with the origin and rising again into birth, he becomes the jnani of light and stays pure.
verse.nuance: Caste (சாதிபேதம்) is listed among the forms the one took, so it is neither denied nor honoured here; 1098 and 1100 attack it. Line 3 is hard: who stays with the origin and is born again, the one or the soul, and whether the jnani is the one returned.

finding.claim: Indian groups descend from a mixture of ancestral populations, and widespread intermarriage gave way to strict endogamy only about 1,900 to 4,200 years ago.

verse.reading: What preceded Hari is the letter A; what stood within Hari is the five letters; what preceded holding is the five letters; and what stood within the breath-horse is the five letters.
verse.nuance: The stanza turns on அரி, which is Hari, Vishnu, but in cipher can be the sun or the letter; வாசிப்பரி is the horse that is the breath. Tradition takes the stanza to place the five letters in the breath, so that the mantra is breathed rather than said. தரிக்கும் (holding, or bearing) is unclear.

finding.claim: Breathing voluntarily at about six breaths a minute raises vagally mediated heart-rate variability during practice, right after one session and after multi-session training.

verse.reading: Taking a body of eight spans, what of it, my Lord? Removing the nearness of women, there is great bliss; so that the eye may see, without the body ceasing, the knowledge that gains siddhi, the siddhi of yoga ... decree: think on it.
verse.nuance: தேகம் ஒழியாமல் சித்தி பெறும் ஞானம், the knowledge that gains siddhi without the body ceasing, is the text's statement of its goal: release in the living body. போசைவிதி is an obscure word, perhaps a corruption; the sense of the last foot is lost.

finding.claim: Loving-kindness and compassion meditation improve self-reported wellbeing and reduce distress in small to moderate degree.

verse.reading: We will shut the snake in the pot of ம, we have scooped up and eaten the breath of the jewelled circle, we will push away the pots of வ, leap past the crooked dream, let it dance in the open sea of space, offer the five instruments as sacrifice, and saying we stand become the form of சி, see the holy feet, be clear and dance.
verse.nuance: The letters are those of the five-letter mantra: in the usual Saiva reading ம stands for mala or the body, வ for grace, சி for Siva. The snake begins in ம and ends as சி, so the stanza is a passage through நமசிவாய from bond to Siva. பஞ்ச கருவி are the five senses, and வாசி is the breath as practice.

finding.claim: Curcumin, though popular, is unstable, poorly absorbed and a frequent false positive in assays, and no double-blind trial has shown a clear therapeutic benefit.

verse.reading: Once the Lord who is everywhere has entered our body, they still parcel him into shares and will not come near the hard way. 'Our god, your god': are there two? The difference is yours alone; in truth there is no second.
verse.nuance: பங்கு கூறு போடுவார், they divide into shares, is said of the sectarians who split the one Lord; பாடு சென்று அணுகிலார் may mean they will not approach the labour of the path, or will not approach the body where he is. The verse's claim is not that the gods are equal but that there is one, and that the two are made by the speakers.

finding.claim: Loophole-free Bell tests confirm that entangled particles show correlations no local hidden-variable theory can explain, though these cannot be used to send signals.

verse.reading: Of that twenty-one thousand six hundred measures of paddy, did any capital come back once it was seen? Of it he seized one part in three as his share, jnana girl.
verse.nuance: 21,600 is the yogic count of breaths in a day and night, so the paddy is the breath and the one-third seized is the share lost, which tradition explains as the breath that goes out beyond the nose and is wasted. The stanza asks whether any 'capital' (முதல்) is recovered from it.

finding.claim: Breathing voluntarily at about six breaths a minute raises vagally mediated heart-rate variability during practice, right after one session and after multi-session training.

verse.reading: Where the four inner instruments and the five senses they govern become one and stand composed, heart, you joined.
verse.nuance: நாலுவகைக் கரணம் are the four inner instruments (mind, intellect, will and ego) of the tattva scheme; நல்கு புலனைந்து are the five senses they give rise to or direct. The nine are not destroyed but made one and steadied (சீலமுற்று), which keeps the body's apparatus inside the union.

finding.claim: Experienced meditators are not reliably better than non-meditators at detecting their own heartbeats, despite reporting greater bodily awareness.

verse.reading: Milk the milk that does not go bad; milk so as to live on day after day; milk the milk that flows without ceasing; milk the milk that grows in the skull.
verse.nuance: தலை மண்டை, the skull, names the source directly; the three qualities (not stinking, unceasing, giving long life) are the tradition's claims for the inner nectar against the body's milk, which sours.

finding.claim: The idea that a fixed stock of breaths or heartbeats sets lifespan rests on a cross-species correlation; within humans, lower resting heart rate predicts lower mortality but slowing breath has not been shown to extend life.

verse.reading: Staying put, kindling the root fire's heat with the breath, so that the honey's chamber opens and one sweetness is tasted; with the three moons from the sky entered into the staff: the yogi who takes this measure while still in the flesh is a yogi indeed.
verse.nuance: The sequence is the standard one of Siddhar yoga: breath heats the fire at the root, the nectar's chamber (தேன் அறை) in the head opens, and sweetness is tasted. மதியம் மூன்று (three moons) and தண்டலம் (the staff's ground, taken as the spine) are the coded terms; the three may be the three kalas of the moon or three centres. ஊனிருந்து, 'while in the flesh', insists that the measure is taken in this body.

finding.claim: Trained practitioners of breathing and cold exposure or of tummo meditation can voluntarily raise body temperature or modulate the innate immune response, effects once thought impossible.

verse.reading: He of unchanging fame and the honey garland, the Siva-yogi of silence who does not open his mouth to rage; and straight (2197) his guru is Chitrambalavan.
verse.nuance: வாய்திறந்து சீறாத: silence is defined as not opening the mouth in anger, a narrower and more practical mounam than the stilling of all thought. Yet 2194 gave him fury; the anger is turned on the disciples' enemies, not spoken.

finding.claim: Meditation is associated with reduced activity in the default mode network and changed coupling between it and attention and control networks, with larger effects in experienced practitioners.

verse.reading: With 'he' and 'I' gone, never forgetting the guru's grace, the poet knew himself by himself; he stayed in nishtai, the fleshly body not perishing, in the state where the eye that reached it does not sleep.
verse.nuance: என்னை என்னால் அறிந்தேன், knowing oneself by oneself, repeats 2317. ஊனுடல் அழியாமல் is the siddha claim that the body is preserved in trance or beyond it; set against 2315's false cage, it shows the two Siddhar attitudes to the body side by side in one song. துயிலாத விழி is the open-eyed absorption, as tradition describes it.

finding.claim: Loss of the sense of self in deep meditation and high-dose psychedelic states takes several distinct forms and is mostly reported by very experienced meditators or at high doses.

verse.reading: When will anger die, speech and action die, the 'I' die, the mind die, and the state of release come and be reached?
verse.nuance: This unit comes from a different printed source and completes the chain of மாண்டு begun in 86: anger, speech, deed, I, mind, each dying in turn, with release as what arrives of itself when they are gone. The 'I' (நான்) dies before the mind.

finding.claim: Mouse studies reported that sleep increases clearance of brain waste through the glymphatic system, but a 2024 study found clearance fell during sleep, so the claim is disputed.

verse.reading: Whoever wanders, demon, do not you wander; even if the town wanders, seek nothing.
verse.nuance: அலைதல் (wandering, restlessness) is the demon's native motion; the stanza sets the mind's stillness against the crowd's. ஒன்றையும் நாடாதே, seek nothing, is repeated in 1699 and matches 1665's 'join with nothing'.

finding.claim: People's minds wander nearly half their waking time, and they report being less happy while wandering than while focused.

verse.reading: What is it that stands settled as the first of the five letters? What is it you chant, standing in the letter of the heart? What is it that the sword of the five letters cuts? You must separate out and tell the straight truth of the unripe letter.
verse.nuance: Three questions on the mantra's inside: its first (ஆதி), its place (நெஞ்சு), its work (அறுப்பு, cutting, as a sword). பிஞ்செழுத்து, the unripe or budding letter, is obscure, perhaps the seed-syllable or the letter before it is sounded; 1142's flower without a bud may be its pair.

finding.claim: Reciting a rosary prayer or a yoga mantra slows breathing to about six a minute and raises baroreflex sensitivity, linking repetitive recitation to the slow-breath physiology.

verse.reading: Serving is the twilight rite of austerity; standing as yoga is bindu and nada; the Sadasiva-waking that agrees with the life-breath is that very place.
verse.nuance: The stanza pairs three terms with three definitions: service with sandhya (தவ சந்தி), yoga with bindu-nada, and the Sadasiva-waking with the breath or soul (ஆவி). சதாசிவ சாக்கிரம் is a yogic state above the practitioner's waking of 2598; the names of the Siva-avasthas in 2685 to 2689 belong to the same scheme.

finding.claim: Much meditation research suffers from vague definitions, small samples and overstated claims, and the evidence for its benefits is weaker than popular accounts suggest.

verse.reading: The cool Karunai Ananda muni, the Varuna who came to be seen and worshipped, the rain-cloud of bliss; and dawn-red (2202) his radiance stands.
verse.nuance: கருணை ஆனந்தமுனி gives the guru a fuller name than the ஆனந்தன் of 2171; the Kural's rain that makes virtue possible becomes the guru raining bliss.

finding.claim: Silent repetition of a single word reduces activity widely across the cortex, including default-mode regions, compared with rest.

verse.reading: With mind on the five letters, son, properly changing them head to foot and foot to head, the deities of the adharas come purely and, as told, stand sweetly in the heart; meditating thus with devotion, firmly smearing ash as the ground, if you do this daily, the unstable gross body becomes stable.
verse.nuance: The promise is kaya-siddhi: the body that does not stay is made to stay by mantra, meditation and ash. ஆதார தேவதைகள் are the presiding deities of the adharas, who are said to take their stand in the heart rather than in their own centres.

finding.claim: Silent repetition of a single word reduces activity widely across the cortex, including default-mode regions, compared with rest.

verse.reading: The poet, whose love and thought go only to the quarrelsome, sinful women whose eyes run to their ears and who play with the sore at their hips, and who has not been granted the fortune of wearing the Lord's two lotus feet, describes his own body as a wilderness where the five thieves raid, a chest of urine and excrement, a casket of the two deeds, a hamlet where wind, bile and phlegm lodge, a bloody frame of filthy skin, a stinking pot, a torn rag of four cubits and nine, a garden of bitter gourd, a mound in the great cremation ground, a top spinning on the rope of desire, a ship of ceaseless disease, a changing illusion, a cage of death, a bellows for rice, a kite flying in the wind, a log that fate's Dharma cuts, a shirt the four-faced tailor stitches, a feast thrown to the pyre, a dry leaf shrivelling in the fire of lust, a tuber worms dig, a forked branch up which the shoot of sin climbs, a lump that walks as a bridegroom and ends lying as a corpse, a burden the town will not let lie, a heap of pulai flowers against the wind, frost before the morning sun, a rainbow moving in the sky, the passing shadow of a thundering cloud, a bubble on water, writing on water, a sight seen in sleep's dream, and, worse than all of these, a stain of maya; and says enough, enough, Lord, enough: show the dance of bliss while the daughter of the mountain cries 'live', take me and rule me, for that is the beauty of your grace.
verse.nuance: The names fall into kinds: the body as a container of waste, as a thing moved by what is not itself (the top on the rope of desire, the kite in the wind, the puppet of 240), as a thing already prepared for death (the log Dharma cuts, the shirt Brahma sews, the feast for the fire), and as the stock brief things, which the poet caps by saying the body is worse than a bubble or a dream because it is a மாயக் களங்கம், a stain made of maya. சதுர்முகப் பாணன், the four-faced tailor, is Brahma stitching the body; விதிவழித் தருமன் is Yama as Dharma. நான்முழத் தொன்பது பீற்றத் துண்டம் is obscure: a torn cloth four cubits long with nine (holes), or nine torn pieces of four cubits. ஊரிற் கிடக்க ஒட்டா உபாதி uses the Siddhanta word உபாதி loosely for the corpse the town hurries out. The petition at the end is brief, and the grace asked for is to be ruled (ஆண்டுகொண்டருள்), not to be released.

finding.claim: Ageing reflects a set of interacting cellular hallmarks such as genomic instability, loss of protein balance and stem-cell exhaustion, none yet reversed in humans.

verse.reading: The root is the circle of the adhara: the three lights, the triangle, the three nadis; the water of the Sivalinga's feet called good conduct; it is the holy feet, the holy body and the dance; holding up all the cosmos with its form, the pillar that has sprouted and looks upward; the whole throat that drank the poison standing as itself: know the letter that begins with A, and see.
verse.nuance: The mooladhara is given its usual marks, the triangle and the three channels (ida, pingala, sushumna); முச்சுடர் (three lights) are sun, moon and fire. கம்பம் (pillar) is the spine or the lingam read as the axis of the body. ஆலமுண்ட கண்டம் is Siva's poison-stained throat, so the body's centres are read as the Lord's own body.

finding.claim: Agreement between practitioners reading the pulse in Ayurvedic and Chinese medicine is low to moderate, and the methods remain poorly standardised.

verse.reading: Full one, who stands as light and comes as fruit, pure, and who recites the teaching that cannot be taught; running like a road and going through the foot of the sky, 'the first Lord is his own lord' has stood for endless time.
verse.nuance: The syntax does not resolve. விண்ணடி, the foot of the sky, is taken in tradition as the crown of the head, where the light passes out. ஆதிநாதன் தன் நாதன் may mean the first Lord is lord even of this light, or that the Lord is his own lord.

finding.claim: Meditators report a wide range of challenging experiences, including perceived lights, altered self-sense, fear and lasting distress, some needing support.

verse.reading: What is the brow-centre: it is the crown of the egg that is Parabrahman; the middle of the nerve named before is fixed as the sushumna; when you drive the mind straight at the uvula, the mind leaps into the sushumna and the five elements merge as one.
verse.nuance: Brow-centre, crown, sushumna and uvula are made one place in four lines; the method is to send the mind, not the tongue or the breath, to the அண்ணாக்கு. This is the verse that 2339 and 2350 enforce.

finding.claim: Meta-analysis of small randomised trials finds alternate-nostril breathing lowers blood pressure modestly, with high heterogeneity between studies.

verse.reading: As a cloud hides the moon, so I, caught in bondage, do not see you.
verse.nuance: The moon is not dimmed by the cloud; the figure puts the obstacle in the seer and leaves the Fullness unchanged. பந்தம், the bond, is the cloud, and the verse does not say what the bond is made of.

finding.claim: Nearly every cell keeps a roughly 24-hour molecular clock entrained by light, and misalignment of these clocks is linked to metabolic and mental illness.

verse.reading: When will I stand contained within the letter a, with the letter va and the letter ma become the sword, and the letter si?
verse.nuance: The letters are those of சிவாயநம: va, ma and si are named, and அவ்வெழுத்து is the letter a (the first of Om, as the Kural's அகர முதல) or 'that letter'. The sword returns from 84: there the five letters together cut the mind, here two of them are the blade and the rest are sheathed in a. Tradition reads such letter-verses as the breath's syllables; the plain sense is the mantra folded into its first sound.

finding.claim: Reciting a rosary prayer or a yoga mantra slows breathing to about six a minute and raises baroreflex sensitivity, linking repetitive recitation to the slow-breath physiology.

verse.reading: Join the stainless mind to the Thing that is seen, as a magnet draws iron and holds it; and in calm, like the pot and its rope, follow without wavering and dance.
verse.nuance: The two images differ: the magnet is attraction that needs no effort, the pot tied to its rope is a bond that does not slip. காட்சியான வஸ்து (the Thing that is seen) makes the object of meditation something already perceived.

finding.claim: Meditation programmes produce moderate improvements in anxiety, depression and pain, with low or no evidence of benefit for attention, mood or sleep beyond active controls.

verse.reading: 'I will do alchemy: silver, and gold finer than the touchstone's gold'; saying 'give gold and coins enough for the guru's bundle', performing tricks and deceiving, they take the property that was handed over and run a league away; even catching sight of them again is rare.
verse.nuance: A plain account of the alchemist's confidence trick: the fee demanded in advance (குருமுடிச்சு, the guru's bundle) and the flight. The verse treats வாதம் (alchemy) as it is practised, a fraud, and says nothing about whether transmutation is possible.

finding.claim: Mercury can be turned into gold only by nuclear reactions such as neutron bombardment of mercury isotopes, never by chemical or alchemical processing.

tamil: ஆசை கொண்ட மாதர் அடைகனவு நீக்கி உன்மேல்
verse.reading: Putting away the dream of desire I have for women, when will I take up the sound of you and subside?
verse.nuance: Desire for women is a dream (கனவு) to be ended; what replaces it is sound (ஓசை), the Lord heard rather than seen, as in 191 and 197.

finding.claim: The brain's dopamine 'wanting' system can drive craving independently of 'liking', so addictive desire can grow while pleasure does not.

verse.reading: If someone seeks out the place where I am and brings food for my hunger with eagerness, I will eat; even if they call me with much insistence I will not go, Hara; even if the body wastes away, from now on I will not go.
verse.nuance: A vow stricter than begging: the poet will not enter a house even when invited, and eats only what is carried to him. ஏகம் இளைத்தாலும், even if the body wastes, accepts starvation as the price, which 407 shows being paid.

finding.claim: Fasting strongly induces autophagy in animal tissues, but direct evidence that it does so in human tissues is sparse.

verse.reading: After the siddhi of the body drove off my karma-deeds, the siddhi of maya and the root whirl will come to me; by the siddhi of the body, by the root tamarind, the first initiation was done; now see it in two years' time.
verse.nuance: காயசித்தி is the deathless or perfected body, and மாயசித்தி here probably the powers over appearance. மூலப் புளி (root tamarind, or root acid) is unexplained; tradition reads புளி in Siddha cipher as a prepared acid or as a body-substance, so the first diksha may be a medicine rather than a rite. The two-year term is the kind of stated period the karpam verses give.

finding.claim: Reported evidence for precognition and other psychic powers failed to replicate and exposed weaknesses in standard statistical practice.

verse.reading: The snake lies inside the anthill, and worldly bondage lies inside the heart; if one subdues bluster and rises, one can watch the horse's show.
verse.nuance: The snake in the anthill is a proverb for a hidden danger, and the stanza pairs it with சக பந்தம் (the world's bond) in the heart; the snake is also kundalini's usual image, so a coded reading has the coiled power waiting in the body as bondage waits in the heart. வீம்பு is boastful stubbornness.

finding.claim: Orch-OR proposes that consciousness arises from quantum computations in neuronal microtubules ending in gravity-related collapse; it remains speculative and is disputed by most physicists and neuroscientists.

verse.reading: I will make known the tvam-pada, which is glory, and the adjuncts that came into it; hear what its nature is: the working of the conscious form told before, girl of knowledge.
verse.nuance: தொம்பதம் is the 'thou' of tat tvam asi, here the individual self considered with its உபாதி, limiting adjuncts. வசித்திரு is read as சித்துரு, the chit-form of 2667; the line is uncertain.

finding.claim: The gut microbiota signals to the brain through immune, endocrine and vagal routes and affects stress responses and behaviour in animals; human causal evidence is still limited.

verse.reading: Making a figure of earth like a wooden puppet and fitting to it the string called the fat living soul, the moment the one who moved it from behind the screen has finished, the body falls; know this clearly and dance.
verse.nuance: The puppet has three parts: the earthen figure, the string that is the jivan, and the hidden mover behind the curtain (திரைக்குள் இருந்து அசைப்போன்). The body falls not when the string breaks but when the mover stops, which places the cause of death in the Lord's will.

finding.claim: Trained practitioners of breathing and cold exposure or of tummo meditation can voluntarily raise body temperature or modulate the innate immune response, effects once thought impossible.

verse.reading: The place where you stayed still, demon, is what was pointed to, I have told you; I do not know what maya this is, and I do not see even myself.
verse.nuance: The repetition of 1679's second half is followed by a confession: the poet does not know what the appearance is and cannot see himself. Not seeing oneself (என்னையும் காணேன்) may be failure or the goal, since 1711 denies the self altogether.

finding.claim: Orch-OR proposes that consciousness arises from quantum computations in neuronal microtubules ending in gravity-related collapse; it remains speculative and is disputed by most physicists and neuroscientists.

verse.reading: Pus, blood, rich fluid and slime pressed together and rising and flowing, when there is not even a cloth to cover it, day and night; the womb that flies and ants enter: for the humans who die day and night there is no medicine to keep them from dying.
verse.nuance: The syntax is broken across the lines and the verse may be corrupt: the yoni in line 3 is where flies and ants enter, which can be the womb one is born from or the dead body's orifices. The close is a direct denial of the medical Siddhars' claim: there is no remedy against death.

finding.claim: The body replaces around 330 billion cells a day, mostly blood and gut cells, so its material is continually renewed.

verse.reading: Whoever wanders, demon, do not you wander; even if the town wanders, seek nothing.
verse.nuance: அலைதல் (wandering, restlessness) is the demon's native motion; the stanza sets the mind's stillness against the crowd's. ஒன்றையும் நாடாதே, seek nothing, is repeated in 1699 and matches 1665's 'join with nothing'.

finding.claim: Meditation is associated with reduced activity in the default mode network and changed coupling between it and attention and control networks, with larger effects in experienced practitioners.

verse.reading: Not knowing the alchemy, saying 'we practise rasavaadham', they put mercury and sulphur in the crucible; will gold grow from it, girl?
verse.nuance: சூதம் (mercury) and கெந்தி (sulphur) are the base pair of Siddha alchemy; the stanza does not deny transmutation, it denies that heating the two without the knowledge (வாதம்) yields it. The claim is historical, that practitioners of the time did exactly this.

finding.claim: Mercury can be turned into gold only by nuclear reactions such as neutron bombardment of mercury isotopes, never by chemical or alchemical processing.

verse.reading: They bend their effort to melting the lingam, not knowing the lingam of the right kind; the tale of joining lead with gold, is it not a disgrace, girl?
verse.nuance: லிங்கம் here is the alchemists' word for cinnabar (ரசலிங்கம், சாதிலிங்கம், red sulphide of mercury), and சாதிலிங்கம் is that mineral's name; the stanza plays on the word's other sense, Siva's emblem, so a second reading has them melting idols while not knowing the true linga. வங்கம் is lead or tin, and the gold-and-lead story is the coiner's fraud.

finding.claim: Mercury can be turned into gold only by nuclear reactions such as neutron bombardment of mercury isotopes, never by chemical or alchemical processing.

verse.reading: The world is imagination, an expanse produced by the inner faculties, a dream, an Indra's net; if on that day it appears so, that is favourable to the subtle.
verse.nuance: அந்தக்கரணம், the inner faculties (mind, intellect, ego, will), are made the producers of the world, which is Vedanta's idealism; இந்த்ரசாலம் is the conjuror's show. The last line is obscure: perhaps that once the world has appeared as dream, the subtle is in reach. 2291 returns to the faculties and says their play cannot be pushed away.

finding.claim: On the predictive-processing account, perception is the brain's best guess about the causes of sensory input, constantly corrected by prediction error.

verse.reading: Listen, son Vasimuni: in the thousand verses he gave earlier he told truly the drugs, salts, bound and melted substances and the way of gems, without a lie; in this book he will tell all the silence in order, so listen bowing.
verse.nuance: The disciple is வாசிமுனி, the breath-sage, and later வாசிநாதா; the name makes the pupil the breath itself. The earlier ஆயிரம் is an alchemical work claimed as Kakapusundar's; the verse marks the turn from alchemy to மவுனம், which the formulas of 2397 to 2403 then undo.

finding.claim: Reciting a rosary prayer or a yoga mantra slows breathing to about six a minute and raises baroreflex sensitivity, linking repetitive recitation to the slow-breath physiology.

verse.reading: Prey for kites, feast for vultures, twist made by the vain one with the water pot, dwelling where worms come to stay, carcass without any good, bondage that even the mother who bore it will not touch once the instruments go slack: I have carried you, and what pleasure is there in you for me?
verse.nuance: கமண்டல வீணன் is Brahma with his water pot, called a wastrel for making this body; முடக்கு, a bend or twist, is the crooked thing he made. கருவி, the instruments, are the senses and organs; when they fail the body becomes untouchable even to its mother. Addressed to the body, as 354 and 375 are.

finding.claim: A typical human body holds roughly as many bacterial cells as human cells, so the body is in large part a community of other organisms.

verse.reading: If you know the state of the breath, the mind, pleased that tapas is accomplished, mounts the horse called தேசி and makes its search; know that, blissful girl.
verse.nuance: The horse is the Siddhars' standing figure for the breath, and tradition hears வாசி itself as the horse; தேசி (shining, or of the country) is the horse's name here. The claim is that knowing the breath is the whole of tapas (தவம் வாய்த்தது), a stronger claim than 2114, where tapas is known through jnana.

finding.claim: Breathing voluntarily at about six breaths a minute raises vagally mediated heart-rate variability during practice, right after one session and after multi-session training.
